page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel processor configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The server includes 32 GB of system memory, providing a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. It does not include bundled local NVMe SSD storage, requiring external persistent network storage, and contains zero GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying Intel processor incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache along with support for advanced instruction set extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. Benchmark results place its single-core stress-ng score at 1676.09 and multi-core score at 6902.54, both falling into average performance bands. The instance achieved 9.71 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a static web serving throughput of 12.95 GB/sec, matching typical performance profiles for its core count.

Performance limitations appear in memory bandwidth and multi-threaded decompression tests, where the PassMark memory score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression were measured in lower performance bands. Large model LLM text generation is restricted, registering 6.31 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model. From a resource perspective, the instance provides cost-effective baseline computing for standard web services, application backends, software build pipelines, and relational database hosting where extreme local storage IOPS are not required.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose instance featuring 8 vCPUs across 4 physical Intel x86_64 cores, 32 GB of system RAM, and no integrated local storage or GPU accelerators. Operating on dedicated CPU hardware, it features 260 MB of L3 cache and supports specialized vector and matrix instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Synthetic benchmarks place the instance within average ranges for single-core and multi-core computing, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 6838.0 and a Redis throughput of 9.71 million SET operations per second. Hardware tradeoffs include lower relative memory bandwidth efficiency, as evidenced by a PassMark memory score in the bottom quartile, along with limited speed during 7B parameter LLM text generation. Overall, the server offers efficient balanced resources for general-purpose web serving, containerized application microservices, software compilation, and standard database instances relying on attached network block storage.
